Request for Comments Concerning Proposed Modification of Section 301 Action on Brazil's Acts, Policies, and Practices Related to Digital Trade and Electronic Payment Services; Unfair, Preferential Tariffs; Anti-Corruption Enforcement; Intellectual Property Protection; Ethanol Market Access; and Illegal Deforestation
abstract: The United States Trade Representative (Trade Representative) proposes a modification of the tariff action taken in connection with the Section 301 investigation of Brazil's acts, policies, and practices related to digital trade and electronic payment services; unfair, preferential tariffs; anti-corruption enforcement; intellectual property protection; ethanol market access; and illegal deforestation. Brazil has made insufficient progress in eliminating the acts, policies, and practices USTR identified as actionable. The proposed modification to duties on certain sugar products and finished aircraft seeks to create additional leverage to encourage Brazil to eliminate its acts, policies, and practices identified as actionable in the investigation. USTR is seeking public comment and will hold a public hearing regarding this proposed modification.

abstract: On November 10, 2026, the U.S. Court of International Trade (CIT) issued its final judgment in American Brass Rod Fair Trade Coalition and its Individual Members v. United States, Consol. title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With a Section 4(d) Rule for Blanding's Turtle
abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Blanding's turtle (Emydoidea blandingii), a reptile species from 14 States in the midwestern and eastern regions of the United States and 3 Provinces in eastern Canada, as a threatened species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Blanding's turtle. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not prudent.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for the Cascade and Columbia Torrent Salamanders
abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Cascade torrent salamander (Rhyacotriton cascadae), a species endemic to the western slope of the Cascade Range in Washington and Oregon, and the Columbia torrent salamander (Rhyacotriton kezeri), a species endemic to the Coast Range in Washington and Oregon, as threatened species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Cascade torrent salamander and the Columbia torrent salamander. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing these species is warranted. Accordingly, we propose to list the Cascade torrent salamander and Columbia torrent salamander as threatened species with a rule issued under section 4(d) of the Act ("4(d) rule"). If finalized as proposed, this rulemaking action would add these species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the two species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.

Extending Deadlines for Submissions by Importers of Automobiles Qualifying for Preferential Tariff Treatment Under the USMCA To Determine U.S. Content
abstract: In Proclamation 10908 of March 26, 2025, "Adjusting Imports of Automobiles and Automobile Parts Into the United States," the President imposed additional tariffs on imports of specified automobiles and automobile parts to eliminate the threat to national security posed by such imports. That Proclamation also provided that importers of automobiles that qualify for preferential tariff treatment under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) may submit documentation to the Secretary of Commerce (Secretary) identifying the amount of U.S. content in each model imported into the United States. In a Federal Register Notice published on May 20, 2025, "Procedures for Submission by Importers of Automobiles Qualifying for Preferential Tariff Treatment Under the USMCA to Determine U.S. Content," the Department of Commerce (Department) established procedures for submission and review of such documentation. The Department amended the submission timelines outlined in those procedures in a Federal Register Notice published on August 19 "Amending Procedures for Submissions by Importers of Automobiles Qualifying for Preferential Tariff Treatment Under the USMCA To Determine U.S. Content." This Notice extends the submission deadlines provided in that Federal Register Notice.

title: Technical Updates to the RCRA Hazardous Waste Permitting Regulations-Permitting Technical Updates Rule
abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing technical updates to the regulations implementing the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) governing hazardous waste treatment, storage, and disposal facilities (TSDFs), as well as associated permitting requirements. The proposal also includes a few conforming technical updates to the generator and transporter regulations. The RCRA hazardous waste TSDF permitting regulations have remained largely unchanged for over three decades, despite evolving standards and practices. Collectively, these revisions are intended to address inadvertent errors, remove obsolete references, reflect current information and standards, and implement targeted updates to the RCRA permitting regulations to improve clarity, consistency, and efficiency in the hazardous waste TSDF permitting program. Through a separate Federal Register document, EPA will be seeking input on areas in the RCRA permitting program and permitting regulations to consider for permitting policy or regulatory reform. This proposed rule helps clear the way for potential future regulatory actions that could improve implementation of the RCRA hazardous waste permitting program. It serves as a maintenance action and does not preclude the possibility of future permitting reform.

title: Significant New Use Rule on a Chemical Substance (P-24-195)
abstract: EPA is proposing a significant new use rule (SNUR) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for a chemical substance that was the subject of a premanufacture notice (PMN) and is also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. The SNUR requires persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of this chemical substance for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification; made an appropriate determination regarding that notification; and taken such actions as required by that determination.

title: Petition for Rulemaking To Consider Amendments to Regulations Governing Interim Use of Rights-of-Way as Trails
abstract: The Board partially grants a petition for rulemaking and proposes amendments to its regulations implementing section 208 of the National Trails System Act Amendments of 1983 to streamline the railbanking process. Under the proposal, the Board would no longer issue Notices or Certificates of Interim Trail Use during trail-use negotiations. Only after an agreement is reached would the Board issue an order authorizing transfer to the trail sponsor. Abandonment authority would no longer be prerequisite to railbanking. The Board would also confirm that by authorizing transfer the Board is not exercising any power of eminent domain or authorizing a taking.

abstract: The U.S. Department of Commerce (Commerce) preliminarily determines on a country-wide basis that imports of certain corrosion- resistant steel products (CORE) completed in Indonesia using cold- rolled steel (CRS) manufactured in the Socialist Republic of Vietnam (Vietnam) are not circumventing the antidumping duty (AD) and countervailing duty (CVD) orders on CORE from Vietnam. The period of inquiry is January 1, 2025, through December 31, 2025. Interested parties are invited to comment on this preliminary determination.

title: Certain Corrosion-Resistant Steel Products From the People's Republic of China: Preliminary Negative Determination of Circumvention of the Antidumping Duty and Countervailing Duty Orders

title: Bonneville Power Administration; Notice of Filing
Oil and Gas and Sulfur Operations in the Outer Continental Shelf-Documents Incorporated by Reference
abstract: The Department of the Interior (DOI or Department), through Marine Minerals Administration (MMA), is incorporating by reference a collection of production measurement industry standards and safety industry standards into its regulations governing oil, gas, and sulfur operations on the Outer Continental Shelf (OCS). Incorporation of these documents by reference will provide industry with up-to-date, minimum requirements for measuring oil and gas production volumes and enhancing safety. Compliance with these standards will reduce uncertainty in the measurement of oil and gas production and update the minimum standards in the safety regulations.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Threatened Species Status With Section 4(d) Rule for White Sands Pupfish and Critical Habitat Determination
abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the White Sands pupfish (Cyprinodon tularosa), a fish species from southcentral New Mexico, as a threatened species with protective regulations under section 4(d) of the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the White Sands pupfish. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. All areas meeting the definition of critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish occur on Department of War (DoW) owned facilities and are exempt from designation as critical habitat in accordance with section 4(a)(3)(B) of the Act. Therefore, we are not proposing any areas as critical habitat for the White Sands pupfish.

title: Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and Plants; Endangered Species Status for Mazama Newt
abstract: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service), propose to list the Mazama newt (Taricha granulosa mazamae), an amphibian species from the Crater Lake caldera in Crater Lake National Park in Klamath County, Oregon, as an endangered species under the Endangered Species Act of 1973, as amended (Act). This determination also serves as our 12-month finding on a petition to list the Mazama newt. After a review of the best scientific and commercial data available, we find that listing the species is warranted. If we finalize this rule as proposed, it would add this species to the List of Endangered and Threatened Wildlife and extend the Act's protections to the species. We find that designating critical habitat for this species is not determinable at this time.

title: Housing and Community Development Act of 1980: Verification of Eligible Status
abstract: This final rule revises HUD's Section 214 regulations to require the verification of U.S. citizenship or the eligible immigration status of all applicants and recipients of assistance under a covered program regardless of age. The rule will also make prorated assistance a temporary condition pending verification of eligible status of all family members, where permitted by statute, as opposed to under HUD's current regulations where prorated assistance could continue indefinitely. These amendments bring HUD's regulations into greater alignment with the wording and purpose of Section 214 and align with the current Administration's priorities and regulatory reform efforts.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; CY 2027 Payment Policies Under the Physician Fee Schedule and Other Changes to Part B Payment and Coverage Policies; Medicare Shared Savings Program Requirements; and Medicare Prescription Drug Inflation Rebate Program
abstract: This final rule addresses: changes to the physician fee schedule (PFS); other changes to Medicare Part B payment policies to ensure that payment systems are updated to reflect changes in medical practice, relative value of services, and changes in the statute; codification of establishment of new policies for: the Medicare Prescription Drug Inflation Rebate Program under the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022; limiting Medicare coverage of certain individuals; the Ambulatory Specialty Model; updates to drugs and biological products paid under Part B; Medicare Shared Savings Program requirements; updates to the Quality Payment Program; updates to policies for Rural Health Clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers; update to the Ambulance Fee Schedule regulations; codification of the Inflation Reduction Act and Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 provisions; updates to Clinical Laboratory Fee Schedule regulations; updates to the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program.

title: Medicare Program: Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment and Ambulatory Surgical Center Payment Systems; and Quality Reporting Programs; including the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Program; Request for Information on Strengthening the Standardization and Comparability of Hospital Price Transparency (HPT) Data; Prior Authorization; Accrediting Organization (AO) Deeming for Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA); and Notices of Closure of Teaching Hospitals and Opportunities To Apply for Available Slots
abstract: This final rule with comment period revises the Medicare Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) and the Medicare Ambulatory Surgical Center (ASC) payment system for calendar year 2027 based on our continuing experience with these systems. We also describe the changes to the amounts and factors used to determine the payment rates for Medicare services paid under the OPPS and those paid under the ASC payment systems. In addition, this final rule with comment period updates and refines the requirements for the Hospital Outpatient Quality Reporting Program and the Ambulatory Surgical Center Quality Reporting Program. There are no changes to the Rural Emergency Hospital Quality Reporting Program. We finalized the expansion of the prior authorization requirement to include additional Botulinum Toxin Injection services. We also finalized implementation of certain provisions of the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, for off-campus outpatient departments of a provider. In addition, this final rule with comment period announces notices of closure of teaching hospitals and opportunities to apply for available slots. Additionally, we finalized the policy that hospital accrediting organizations (AOs) with deeming authority may assess compliance with certain Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act (EMTALA) administrative requirements under 42 CFR 489.20 during accreditation and reaccreditation surveys.

title: Order Renewing Order Temporarily Denying Export Privileges
Outbound Investment Security Program Regulations
abstract: This proposed rule sets forth regulations that would implement Subtitle C of the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act, which is codified at Title VIII of the Defense Production Act. The proposed rule would require United States persons to provide notification to the U.S. Department of the Treasury regarding certain transactions involving foreign persons that are engaged in notifiable technologies; and prohibit United States persons from engaging in certain other transactions involving foreign persons that are engaged in prohibited technologies. Where consistent with Title VIII, the proposed rule incorporates certain definitions and concepts from the current regulations governing the Outbound Investment Security Program. The proposed rule also would add applicability dates to the regulations, such that those regulations would continue to apply to activities that occurred within the relevant timeframe.

title: Notice of Agreements Filed
Request for Information for 2028 Department of Defense (DoD) State Priorities Impacting Service Members and Their Families
abstract: On Tuesday, March 24, 2026, the Department of Defense (referred to herein as "the Department", "Department of War" or DoW") published a request for information in the Federal Register (FR) that provided an opportunity for the public to submit issues that have an impact on service members and their families, where state governments are the primary agents for making positive change. Each year, DoW selects state policy priorities for states to consider that represent barriers resulting from the transience and uncertainty of military life. For example, DoW has asked states to consider remedies that trade residency-based and time-in-state requirements for portability and continuity, including interstate compacts, license reciprocity, credit for military training, spouse unemployment compensation; cross- reporting agreements with child welfare agencies; educational opportunities including advance enrollment, homeschool solutions, in- state tuition, records transfer, and waiver waitlist retention for families with special needs; support for severely injured personnel; custody and juvenile justice protections for deployed parents and military-connected youth; information sharing on military protective orders; employment and legal protections for military families; and predatory lending safeguards. DoW will consider public submissions in setting those priorities.
